answer:
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) works by exploiting client-side vulnerabilities to inject malicious scripts into a user's browser. An attacker can achieve this by placing a script in user-generated content sites, such as bulletin boards or blogs, which are then echoed back to other users' browsers. This allows the attacker to execute scripts in the context of the victim's session, potentially leading to unauthorized actions or data theft [Source 1]. 

The process typically involves identifying potential entry points for XSS vulnerabilities and injecting various script payloads to test if these points can be exploited [Source 2].
